correctness.rationale: The common-height rooted-PD definition makes singleton samples constant and two-taxon samples at least height H. At N-1, omission of a nonsingleton changes neither statistic, and omission of a singleton decreases both. Hypergeometric probabilities for the unique doubleton give the exact covariance identity with positive denominators and a nonempty strict negative-length interval at every interior m. A single length choice works at all \(3\le m\le N-2\). Exact subset enumeration independently reproduced 72 cases and the \(N=5\), \(-3/200\) witness; universality rests on the direct proof.

value.rationale: The fixed-sampling-depth joint relation of taxonomic richness and phylogenetic diversity is ecologically natural and not determined by each quantity being monotone in sampling effort. The all-depth universal-vs-attainable sign classification, sharp \(N=5\) onset, and one common counterexample negative at every admissible interior depth give a strong structural boundary with an explicit biologically interpretable branch-length threshold. It is not a known-table recomputation or an arbitrary isolated parameter slice.
